draft.title: The war in the Pacific
card: On 7 December 1941, Japan launched a surprise air attack on the United States naval base at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii. The United States declared war on Japan the next day.
Japan also attacked British, Dutch and American territories in South-East Asia. It took Malaya, the Dutch East Indies and the Philippines, and Singapore fell in February 1942.
Japan's forces then moved south towards Australia. Darwin was bombed on 19 February 1942, the first of many air raids on northern Australia.
The fall of Singapore, a major British base, was a shock to Australians. Many Australian soldiers were taken prisoner there, and the government turned to the United States for protection.
draft.remember: Pearl Harbor brought the United States in, and Japan's fast advance brought the war close to Australia.

a.q: What was the immediate result of Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor?
opts: The United States went to war against Japan
Japan captured Singapore from the British
Darwin was bombed by Japanese aircraft
Australia declared war on Germany
a.why: The attack on a United States base led the United States to declare war on Japan the next day. Singapore fell and Darwin was bombed, but these came later in the Japanese advance. Australia had joined the war in 1939.
a.clue: Think about whose naval base was hit.

b.q: Why did the fall of Singapore in February 1942 alarm many Australians?
opts: It showed Japan's advance was close to Australia
It showed the United States had left the war
It meant Japan had already invaded Australia
It ended the British Empire's war with Germany
b.why: Singapore was a major British base, and its fall showed Japan's forces were moving fast towards Australia. Japan had bombed Darwin but had not invaded the mainland, so the option about an invasion is wrong.
b.clue: Look at where Japan was heading next.

a.best: The United States went to war against Japan

b.best: It showed Japan's advance was close to Australia

problems.detail: The why says 'Japan had bombed Darwin' when explaining the alarm over Singapore's fall. Singapore fell on 15 February 1942 and Darwin was bombed on 19 February, so Darwin had not been bombed yet when Singapore fell. This sequence could mislead students.

'It took Malaya, the Dutch East Indies and the Philippines, and Singapore fell in February 1942' suggests all of these fell by February 1942. The Dutch East Indies fell in March 1942 and the Philippines in May 1942, both after Singapore.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The why for (b) wrongly implies Darwin was bombed before Singapore fell, and the card's list of Japanese conquests blurs the order in which they fell.
